tasks.name: Apply prioritization framework to rank items
tasks.description: Use WSJF or MoSCoW to rank backlog items.
steps: 1. Confirm the ranking scope covers all Ready items in Jira
2. Enter the business value score on each Ready item in Jira
3. Enter the time criticality score on each Ready item in Jira
4. Enter the risk reduction score on each Ready item in Jira
5. Enter the job size estimate on each Ready item in Jira
6. Compute the WSJF score on each Ready item in Jira
7. Resolve ranking ties among the top 10 items in Jira
8. Flag items lacking WSJF inputs as Needs Refinement in Jira
9. Record the rationale for any priority override in the item comments in Jira
10. Export the ranked order snapshot to the planning page in Confluence
11. Reconcile the ranked item count to the Ready item count in Jira
12. Record the Product Owner sign-off on the ranked backlog in Jira

keys.oldValue: The team's product backlog for the current planning cycle; scope = all ready backlog items in the Jira project being ranked via WSJF (or MoSCoW), covering the next 2-3 sprints of candidate work.
Applied each sprint at backlog refinement and at quarterly PI planning; scores re-validated when new items enter 'Ready'.
ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
Product Owner

Every ranked item has the WSJF inputs populated (business value, time criticality, risk reduction, job size) or a MoSCoW label; 100% of 'Ready' items have a computed rank; 0 items ranked without a job-size estimate.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Count of ranked items reconciles to the count of 'Ready' items in the Jira board; WSJF ordering is a strict total order (no ties left unresolved for the top 10).
Ranking captured in Jira custom fields (WSJF score) with change history; a snapshot of the prioritized order exported to Confluence per planning cycle, timestamped.
Items lacking inputs are flagged 'Needs Refinement' and excluded from ranking until complete; a priority override against WSJF requires Product Owner rationale recorded in the item's comments.

All 'Ready' backlog items in the planning cycle (typically 20-60 items).

Mismatches corrected in Jira and re-ranked; disputed inputs escalated to the Product Owner; overrides documented with rationale.
Approved method = WSJF per the team's SAFe/agile playbook v-current (or MoSCoW where explicitly chosen); method recorded in the planning page.
Parameter source = the WSJF component scores agreed by the team during refinement (Fibonacci relative sizing), stored in the Jira item fields.

steps: 1. Set the title field in each page's frontmatter in GitHub Enterprise
2. Set the owning team field in each page's frontmatter in GitHub Enterprise
3. Set the source repo path in each page's frontmatter in GitHub Enterprise
4. Set the last-reviewed date in each page's frontmatter in GitHub Enterprise
5. Set the release version in each page's frontmatter in GitHub Enterprise
6. Validate frontmatter against the schema in GitHub Actions
7. Run the broken-link check on the docs build in GitHub Actions
8. Reconcile rendered pages to source files in the build manifest in GitHub Actions
9. Publish the docs within 2 business days of the release tag in Backstage
10. Verify every page resolves at its portal URL in Backstage
11. Log each failing page as a DOC-DEFECT in Jira
12. Attach the portal URL to the release ticket in Jira
13. Store the publish log with the artifact hash in GitHub Actions
14. Obtain the review approval on the docs pull request in GitHub Enterprise

keys.oldValue: All net-new and materially changed developer-facing docs for the current release: README, API reference (OpenAPI), architecture (C4/ADRs), runbooks and onboarding guide for repos merged to main this sprint. Excludes third-party vendor docs and archived (deprecated) service pages.
Current release train (2-week sprint boundary); docs must be published within 2 business days of the release tag (e.g. v2025.07.0) being cut.
source code/CI-CD repository
Software Engineer

Each portal page carries frontmatter: title, owning team, source repo/path, last-reviewed date, and release version. Broken-link check passes with 0 dead internal links; all code samples reference a resolvable module/endpoint.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Count of published portal pages equals count of docs source files (docs/**/*.md) in the release tag; portal page count reconciled to the docs-as-code build manifest with 0 variance.
Portal publish CI job stores build log and rendered artifact hash with commit SHA and UTC timestamp in the CI/CD repository artifact store; retained 12 months per release.

Any page failing link-check or missing frontmatter is logged as a Jira ticket type 'DOC-DEFECT', linked to the release; disposition = fixed-and-republished or waived-with-owner-sign-off before release close.
Tech Lead
Software Engineer
All portal pages published for the release under test (typically 20-60 pages per release train).
PASS = 100% of intended docs resolve at their portal URL (HTTP 200), 0 broken internal links, frontmatter complete; FAIL if any intended page returns 404 or link-check reports >0 dead internal links.
Failed publish reverts portal to prior release snapshot; defect raised as Jira 'DOC-DEFECT', owner = Software Engineer, 2-business-day republish SLA before release is marked done.
Portal frontmatter schema defined in docs/_meta/schema.yml: fields title (string), owner (team slug), source (repo#path), lastReviewed (ISO date), version (semver).
Docs build manifest emitted by the CI job lists total source files vs total rendered pages; the two counts must match exactly (0 delta) for the publish step to succeed.

tasks.name: Publish sprint plan to stakeholders
tasks.description: Publish sprint plan and backlog status to stakeholders via the delivery tracking tool.
steps: 1. Confirm an estimate on every committed story in Jira
2. Confirm an assignee on every committed story in Jira
3. Confirm the epic link on every committed story in Jira
4. State the sprint goal on the published plan in Confluence
5. State committed points versus capacity on the plan in Confluence
6. Reconcile committed points to the commitment in PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align)
7. Reconcile the published story count to the board in Jira
8. Publish the plan within 1 business day of planning in Confluence
9. Attach the exported snapshot with the sprint id in Confluence
10. Track each post-publish scope change in PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align)
11. Re-sync any plan discrepancy the same business day in Jira
12. Record the Product Owner sign-off on the plan page in Confluence

keys.oldValue: The current sprint plan and backlog status for the squad: committed stories, capacity, sprint goal, and burndown, published to all named stakeholders (Product Owner, Tech Lead, dependent squads).
The active sprint (e.g. Sprint 2026.07, 2-week iteration); plan published within 1 business day of sprint planning and refreshed at each daily standup.
PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align)
Product Owner
Published plan shows for every committed story: title, estimate, assignee, status, and linkage to epic/PI objective; sprint goal and total committed vs capacity points are stated.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Sum of committed story points on the published plan equals the committed points in Jira Align for the sprint (delta = 0); story count on the shared view matches the Jira board.
Published plan snapshot (Jira Align dashboard link or exported PDF) stored in Confluence with sprint ID and UTC timestamp; each republish is versioned.
Scope changes after publish are tracked as scope-change entries in Jira Align with rationale and PO approval; late additions flagged in the next standup and re-published.
Product Owner
Scrum Master
All committed sprint items in the published plan; 100% must be traceable to a Jira work item.
PASS = published plan reconciles to the Jira board (same items, estimates, statuses) and all stakeholders have access; FAIL = any committed item missing from the published view or points mismatch.
Discrepancy between published plan and board -> Scrum Master re-syncs and republishes within the same business day; recurring drift logged as a process defect in Jira.
Acceptance: plan published to all named stakeholders within 1 business day of planning, reconciles 1:1 with the Jira board, includes sprint goal and capacity.
Confluence 'Sprint Plans' space, page named 'Sprint <id> Plan' with the Jira Align dashboard embed and export attachment.

tasks.name: Rank backlog items
tasks.description: Rank the backlog by value, risk, and dependency order.
steps: 1. Record the WSJF value components on every eligible item in Jira
2. Record a risk rating on every eligible item in Jira
3. Record an estimate on every eligible item in Jira
4. Link dependencies on every eligible item in Jira
5. Exclude unestimated items from the ranked zone in Jira
6. Rank the items with no ties in the top 20 in Jira
7. Reconcile the ranked view count to eligible items in Jira
8. Move each unrankable item to Needs Refinement with a reason in Jira
9. Attach the dated ranked snapshot to the sprint page in Confluence
10. Retain the WSJF scoring sheet on the sprint page in Confluence
11. Record the Product Owner sign-off on the ranking in Jira

keys.oldValue: Scope = the team's product backlog in Jira for the value stream; population = all 'Ready' and 'Refined' backlog items (epics/stories/spikes) eligible for the next 2-3 sprints.
Re-ranked every sprint at backlog refinement and again immediately before sprint planning (2-week cadence).
Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps
Product Owner

Every ranked item has: value/priority score (e.g. WSJF components), risk rating, estimate, dependency links, and a rank order with no ties in the top 20; unestimated items are excluded from the ranked zone.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Count of items in the prioritized backlog view equals the count of 'Ready/Refined' items in Jira (no dropped or duplicated stories); rank is a strict total order over the top slice.
Ranked backlog snapshot exported from Jira after each refinement, dated and versioned, attached to the sprint page in Confluence; WSJF scoring sheet retained.
Items that cannot be ranked (missing estimate, unclear value, blocked by dependency) moved to a 'Needs Refinement' status with owner and reason logged; escalated if blocking for >1 sprint.
Product Owner

tasks.name: Re-prioritize backlog at defined cadence
tasks.description: Review and re-prioritize the backlog on cadence to incorporate new demand and changing priorities.
steps: 1. Filter eligible items in New, Refined or Ready states in Jira
2. Score each eligible item on the WSJF model v1.2 in Jira
3. Rerank the backlog at the sprint-start cadence in Jira
4. Verify the rank order is strictly monotonic in Jira
5. Reconcile pre-session to post-session item counts in Jira
6. Move unscorable items to Needs Refinement with a note in Jira
7. Notify stakeholders of any rank change of 10 or more positions in Jira
8. Pull only items above the capacity cut-line into the sprint in Jira
9. Attach the before-after board snapshots to the cadence page in Confluence
10. Record the reprioritization decision notes on the cadence page in Confluence
11. Complete the independent reasonableness check on the rerank in Jira
12. Record the cadence sign-off on the decision notes in Confluence

keys.oldValue: The team/value-stream backlog in Jira/Jira Align; scope = all items in states 'New', 'Refined', and 'Ready' eligible for reprioritization at the defined cadence, excluding items already in an active sprint.
Reprioritization cadence = start of each 2-week sprint; PI-level reranking each quarterly PI planning.
ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
Product Owner
Each reprioritized item has a priority score (WSJF components: business value, time criticality, risk reduction, job size) populated; the board view blocks 'Ready' without a score.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Backlog item count before and after the session reconciles (no items lost); rank order is strictly monotonic with 0 duplicate rank values.
Board snapshot (before/after) and the reprioritization decision notes exported to Confluence, tagged with the sprint/PI id and UTC timestamp; retained 12 months.
Items that cannot be scored (missing acceptance criteria) moved to 'Needs Refinement' with a note; unresolved after 2 cadences escalated to the Product Owner.
Scrum Master
Prioritization uses the approved WSJF model v1.2 documented in the Agile playbook; scoring rubric referenced in the board's field help.

keys.key: Independent re-performance or reasonableness check completed
keys.oldValue: Product Owner
A rank change of >=10 positions on a committed item triggers stakeholder notification before the sprint commits.
Only items scored >= the cut-line (top of capacity) are pulled into the sprint; below-cut items remain ranked but uncommitted.
Product Owner
All eligible backlog items in New/Refined/Ready at the cadence boundary.
PASS = 100% of top-of-backlog (above cut-line) items carry a WSJF score and acceptance criteria; FAIL = any committed item without a score or with missing acceptance criteria.
Disputes over ranking resolved by the Product Owner as decision authority; unresolvable strategic conflicts escalated to the portfolio Monthly Review.
Acceptance = backlog reranked per WSJF, top items refined with acceptance criteria, and decision notes captured for the cadence.
Evidence = the before/after board snapshots and decision notes in Confluence, linked from the sprint/PI record.

tasks.name: Re-test fixed defects
tasks.description: Re-test defects reported as fixed against the build and update the test evidence with the pass or fail outcome for each. Done when re-test results are recorded.
steps: 1. Queue every defect in Ready for Re-test status in Jira
2. Verify the fix commit SHA matches the merged PR in GitHub Enterprise
3. Record the build tag re-tested against on each defect in Jira
4. Execute the linked test case for each defect in Jira
5. Record the actual result on each re-test execution in Jira
6. Record the pass or fail verdict on each re-test execution in Jira
7. Confirm the pre-fix failure no longer reproduces in Jira
8. Re-run the affected module regression suite in GitHub Actions
9. Attach the execution evidence to each defect in Jira
10. Reopen each failed defect to the fixing developer in Jira
11. Raise a test-blocked ticket for each untestable defect in Jira
12. Reconcile re-test executions to Fixed defects in Jira
13. Re-execute all re-tests after any new build in Jira
14. Record the re-test cycle completion on the release in Jira

keys.oldValue: All defects in Jira with status 'Ready for Re-test' resolved against build artifact of the current release candidate (repo main branch, tagged rc-x.y.z); one re-test execution per defect.
Current sprint window and the active release train cycle (e.g. Sprint 2026.07, Release 26.3), covering all defects moved to 'Fixed' since the last re-test cycle.
ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
QA Analyst

Every re-test record carries: defect key, build/tag re-tested against, test case ID, actual result, pass/fail verdict, tester, and timestamp; no record may be saved without a linked test-case execution.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Count of defects marked 'Fixed' at cycle start reconciles exactly to count of re-test executions recorded (delta = 0); any un-re-tested 'Fixed' defect blocks the release gate.

Re-test evidence (execution log, screenshots, console/API output) attached to the Jira defect and to the Xray/Zephyr test execution, stamped with build tag and UTC timestamp; retained per release for 12 months.

Defects that fail re-test are re-opened, assigned back to the fixing developer with 'reopened' label, and logged in the release exception register; blocked/untestable items get a 'test-blocked' Jira ticket with owner and target date.
Test Lead

For each re-tested defect the failing pre-fix behavior no longer reproduces and the documented expected result is observed on the fixed build; regression suite for the affected module re-run with 0 new failures.
ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
Each re-test links to the originating defect (Jira DEF-#) and to the change/PR that delivered the fix; verify the fix commit SHA in the re-tested build matches the merged PR.
QA Analyst
All defects flagged 'Fixed / Ready for Re-test' in the current release train; 100% must be re-tested, not sampled.

PASS = documented expected result observed and no regression in the module suite; FAIL = original defect reproduces or any new regression appears. Release gate requires 100% of re-tested defects PASS or explicitly deferred with sign-off.
Failed re-test -> re-open defect to developer with reopened label; untestable -> raise 'test-blocked' Jira ticket, owner = QA Lead, resolve within 2 business days or escalate to Release Manager.
Re-test results are valid only for the exact build tag re-tested (rc-x.y.z); a new build supersedes prior re-test evidence and requires re-execution before release.

tasks.name: Refine backlog items to definition of ready
tasks.description: Shape and refine items through estimation sessions to meet the definition of ready.
steps: 1. Write the user-story statement on each item in Jira
2. Record testable acceptance criteria on each item in Jira
3. Record the session estimate on each item in Jira
4. Link identified dependencies on each item in Jira
5. Resolve open blocking questions on each item in Jira
6. Complete the DoR checklist gate before marking Ready in Jira
7. Reconcile Ready items to passing DoR checklists in Jira
8. Keep each blocked item in Refinement with a documented blocker in Jira
9. Archive the refinement session notes to the team page in Confluence
10. Return any story pulled without meeting DoR to the backlog in Jira
11. Record the refinement close-out confirmation on the notes in Confluence

keys.oldValue: Backlog items being refined toward Definition of Ready; scope = all stories/enablers slated for the next 2 sprints on the team's Jira board that are not yet marked 'Ready'.
Refinement covers the next 2 sprints; run weekly at the backlog refinement session.
ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
Product Owner

A story meets DoR when it has a user-story statement, acceptance criteria, an estimate, dependencies identified, and no open blocking questions; the board's DoR checklist gates the transition to 'Ready'.

keys.key: Control totals or record counts reconcile
keys.oldValue: Count of items marked 'Ready' reconciles with items passing all DoR checklist fields; no item is 'Ready' with an unmet DoR field.
Refinement outcomes (estimates, split decisions) recorded on each Jira story with timestamp; refinement session notes archived to the team Confluence page.
Items that cannot reach DoR (open dependency, unclear requirement) stay in 'Refinement' with a documented blocker and follow-up owner on the ticket.
Scrum Master
Scrum Master
All items refined in the session and their DoR checklist state (typically 8-20 stories).
Pass = every story marked 'Ready' has acceptance criteria, an estimate, and 0 open blocking questions; fail = any 'Ready' story missing a DoR field.
A story pulled into sprint without meeting DoR is returned to the backlog and logged as a Jira 'AGILE-Exception', owner = Scrum Master, resolved within 1 business day.
Definition of Ready is met when the story is estimated, has testable acceptance criteria, dependencies are resolved or scheduled, and the team confirms shared understanding at refinement.
DoR state and refinement history recorded on each Jira story; session summary on the team Confluence refinement page.

data catalog/quality tool

tasks.name: Resolve blocking dependencies before sprint commitment

9. Mark stories Ready only when blocking links are cleared in Jira
10. Save the dependency-status snapshot to the planning note in Confluence
11. Record the commitment sign-off on the planning note in Confluence

ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
Scrum Master

Scrum Master

tasks.name: Resolve integration test defects
tasks.description: Resolve defects identified during integration testing and re-verify the fixes. Done when defects are closed and verified.
steps: 1. Filter open Integration Test defects for the release fix version in Jira
2. Record reproduction steps on each defect in Jira
3. Record the root-cause note on each defect in Jira
4. Link the fix pull request on each defect in Jira
5. Merge the fix pull request in GitHub Enterprise
6. Run the targeted integration test for each fix in GitHub Actions
7. Run the full regression for any fix over 200 changed lines in GitHub Actions
8. Run the contract tests against the pinned OpenAPI spec in GitHub Actions
9. Attach the re-test result with the CI run id to each defect in Jira
10. Reconcile Fixed defects to merged PRs with passing re-tests in Jira
11. Disposition any unfixable defect as Deferred with a risk note in Jira
12. Raise an SDLC-Exception for each deferred defect in Jira
